 Former Los Angeles Lakers guard Kobe Bufkin, who spent 2025-26 with the team, joined the Utah Jazz just before the start of the season.
 By Aaron Coloma · October 21, 2026 · 2 min read April 7, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers guard Kobe Bufkin (18) controls the ball against the Oklahoma City Thunder during the first half at Crypto.com Arena. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Former Los Angeles Lakers guard Kobe Bufkin, who spent the 2025-26 season with the team, joined the Utah Jazz just before the start of the 2026-27 season.
 The Jazz are signing Kobe Bufkin, per source, to Utah’s newly-opened two-way slot.
— Jake Fischer (@JakeLFischer) October 21, 2026 Bufkin signed a two-way contract with the Jazz to fill their final two-way spot, almost immediately following the team’s decision to waive Blake Hinson, who signed a two-way contract with the team last season.
 When Did the Lakers Have Kobe Bufkin?
 The 23-year-old played the first two seasons with the Atlanta Hawks, only seeing the floor in 27 NBA games, before they traded him to the Brooklyn Nets, who waived him shortly before the start of the 2025-26 season.
 Los Angeles acquired him Nov. 13, when the G League South Bay Lakers traded for him in exchange for a 2027 first-round pick in the G League draft. Bufkin briefly spent time with the Grizzlies last season in the middle of his Lakers stint after Memphis brought him in on a 10-day hardship deal, but he returned to the South Bay Lakers immediately after.
 Related coverage Lakers Make Ruling on Collin Sexton Amid Leg Injury Read more → He appeared 16 times for the Lakers, making his first NBA start in the process, but only saw the floor for 7.4 minutes per game with the team. He averaged just 2.9 points per game, the lowest in his three-year career, while securing 0.8 rebound and 0.6 assists per game, also career lows.
 The Lakers ultimately waived him on April 10, and he tried his luck with the Pelicans during Summer League and the preseason, but they also waived him Oct. 17.
 April 7, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers guard Kobe Bufkin (18) controls the ball against the Oklahoma City Thunder during the first half at Crypto.com Arena. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Does Kobe Bufkin Fit With the Jazz?
 The Jazz surprisingly have some depth in the guard positions this year after drafting 19-year-old Darryn Peterson out of Kansas this offseason, meaning Bufkin has a ways to go if he wants to feature for the team this year.
 In addition to Peterson, the Jazz have established players like Keynote George, Isaiah Collier and Brice Sensabaugh to fill in their backcourt.
 He has already taken clear steps forward, averaging 21.3 points per game in the Summer League with the Pelicans and dropping 30 points in his debut with the team, but will have to improve even further if he wants to get a proper look in the NBA.
